text: Drop Mount Everest into the ocean. Its peak would still be two kilometres underwater.
Squeeze all that water into one cube, and each side would be eleven hundred kilometres long.
At a hundred metres, blue whales hunt in the last of the sunlight.
At two hundred and ten, we pass USS Triton's limit. The first sub to sail round the world underwater.
At two hundred and fifty-three, one man got here on a single breath. Your lungs aren't built for this.
Whales go deeper. Blue whales reach about five hundred metres. Sperm whales keep going, chasing giant squid.
At seven hundred and thirty, many military subs have to stop. Any deeper, and the hull could crack.
Hang the world's tallest building upside down, and its tip would reach about here.
At one thousand metres, the sunlight is gone. It's night here forever. And yet, something is still alive. That's part two.
